question: {If } sin theta = (3)/(5), { find the value of } cos theta. (theta { is in the first quadrant})
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

sin²θ + cos²θ = 1

⇒ cosθ = √(1 − sin²θ)

= √(1 − (3/5)²) = √(1 − 9/25)

= √(16/25) = 4/5

**∴ Answer = 4/5**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

sinθ = 3/5, θ in first quadrant

**Formula used:**

sin²θ + cos²θ = 1

**Calculation:**

⇒ cos²θ = 1 − sin²θ

⇒ = 1 − (3/5)²

⇒ = 1 − 9/25 = 16/25

⇒ cosθ = √(16/25)

⇒ = 4/5 (positive since first quadrant)

**∴ The correct answer is 4/5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Identity Used

sin²θ + cos²θ = 1

Quadrant Rule

First quadrant ⇒ all ratios positive

Triangle Method

3-4-5 triangle can be used

Key Insight

Always take positive root in first quadrant
